newsitem.title: USA: IPO VIEW - SPECULATIVE US STOCKS GET LEG-UP IN MKT.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW - SPECULATIVE US STOCKS GET LEG-UP IN MKT.

text.p: Sunning in the success of three banner months, the new issues market has become so fetching to investors that it is beginning to make room for more speculative stocks, industry experts said.
"There's so much money flowing, investors are thinking why not just strike while the iron is hot," said Tom Taulli, director of research at IPO Monitor.

Taulli said enthusiasm over initial public offerings was so high that it allowed for a subtle re-emergence of "concept companies"-- businesses he described as low on revenues, typically led by young managers and lacking solid financial performance histories.
Among sectors producing this riskier class of investment, he said, were CD-ROM content developers and small-sized Internet banking service providers.

Taulli stressed, however, that the IPO market is still laden with quality investment opportunities for those looking for solid deals, and that IPOs should continue to thrive as long as fund managers remain bullish on small-capitalization stocks.

Last week's new issues alone generated $1.49 billion, up from the previous week's $801.1 million, according to Securities Data Co. Analysts said Friday's stock market sell-off, which drove the Dow Jones Industrial Average down by 157 points, was unlikely to adversely affect the IPO market.
A revenue-maker, but a potential risk-runner nonetheless, Basham named SL Green Realty Corp, the largest offering slated to price this week.
The real estate investment trust, underwritten by Lehman Brothers, is offering 10 million shares, and is expected to generate $200 million.

"This is a very different kind of REIT," Basham said of SL Green. The company, which acquires and renovates office buildings in Manhattan that are older than 25 years old, relies on a narrow market at a time when other REITs are diversifying, he said.
"If something happens to the New York economy, it could really affect rates," Basham said. "We think this might be a good investment for someone not dependent on a stable dividend."
Manish Shah, editor and publisher of IPO Maven, named Corporate Family Solutions as an up-and-comer among the week's IPO pick.

Underwriters Montgomery Securities posted a pricing range from $8.00 to $10.00 for the onsite child-care provider, but Shah predicted the company would price above range at about $10.50 and open $2.00 above its pricing on its first day of trade.

Within a year, Shah added, the company could well see its stock hit mid-20 levels. "It's a very tightly run company... and many of its customers are Fortune 500 companies," Shah said, such as Boeing Co and Campbell Soup Co.

Shah also forecast that Positron Fiber Systems Corp would open for trade at $1.50 above its pricing, estimated in a $9.00 to $11.00 range. The company, which provides broad band technology, is underwritten by Robertson Stephens & Co.
